title: Edgecase Ontology Mapping and Auto-Patch Recipes
summary: Working doc: build an error ontology for onboarding eval failures and map compact automatic patch recipes that can be executed at the prompt preprocessor layer or as lightweight runtime routing logic. Goal: reduce human triage by 40% on top-20 failure sources.
background: Recent onboarding runs for several open models showed a long tail of low-frequency but high-impact failures. Manual triage is expensive and slow. This doc proposes an explicit ontology (labels + quick heuristics) and a set of small, testable auto-patches (string normalization, prompt scaffolding, dual-funnel prompts, conditional rerouting to conservative model variants). Intended to sit between eval signal ingestion and the remediation playbook so we can run shadow patches and measure effectiveness before shipping to production.
methodology: 1) Sampled 8k failing examples across 5 promptsets (onboarding, chat, assistant, summarization, extraction). 2) Manual labeling into provisional ontology buckets (two annotators + adjudication). 3) Derived lightweight heuristics and minimal rewrite rules for each bucket. 4) Implemented patch prototypes as transformation functions in the eval harness. 5) Ran A/B style shadow tests measuring failure->pass lift and human-review reduction. NOTE: iterations focused on smallest-change patches to minimize semantic drift.
error_clusters: Entity-misalignment: model invents entities or swaps named entities in factual answers; often triggered by underspecified queries or lists with similar tokens
Instruction-ambiguity: multi-intent prompts where the model chooses one intent arbitrarily (e.g., summarize vs. critique), commonly from unlabeled user instruction phrases
Truncation-edge: long-context handling where key tokens at tail become masked or truncated leading to hallucinated completions
Format-violations: model returns free text when a strict JSON/CSV structure is required (broken output parsing downstream)
Safety-misclass: model produces borderline content because of adversarial phrasing or rare entity combinations
Temporal-inconsistency: answers that mix timestamps (e.g., saying an event happened in both 2019 and 2022), typically from noisy corpora examples
Unit-incoherence: numeric units or currencies are swapped (GBP vs USD) when prompt lacks explicit locale context
Extraction-collapse: partial extraction for lists or tables, missing items due to off-by-one token windowing
prompt_archetypes: Shallow-instruction: one-line prompt with no context or constraints
Compound-intent: multiple asks bundled in one turn without enumerated sub-instructions
Loose-format-request: asks for machine-readable output but provides natural-language examples only
Long-context-probe: includes lengthy prior conversation or document and asks for precise extraction
Edge-token-adversarial: contains unusual unicode, brackets, or punctuation that confuses tokenizer
Numerical-precision: prompts that require exact numeric formatting or rounding rules
auto_patch_recipes: Entity-canonicalization: pre-tokenizer pass that maps aliases to canonical IDs (e.g., 'BigCorp' -> 'BigCorp, Inc.'), using a small fuzzy-match dictionary. Low-risk and high yield for entity-misalignment.

Dual-funnel prompting: detect compound-intent archetype and split into 1) explicit enumeration of sub-tasks and 2) a condensed single-task fallback. Route both to the model and merge via simple aggregator heuristics.
Format-stub scaffolding: inject strict JSON skeleton and 2–3 inline examples into prompt for format-violations; fall back to conservative parser if received text doesn't validate.
Context-trim + salient-prefix: compute ROUGE-lite salience on long-context prompts and keep top-k sentences plus a synthesized question-context bullet list to avoid truncation-edge failures.
Punctuation-normalizer: normalize unusual punctuation, collapse repeated whitespace, and remove control chars to mitigate edge-token-adversarial failures.

Unit-disambiguation insertion: if numeric tokens detected and locale unknown, insert '(assume USD unless otherwise specified)' or reverse for markets with known locale; measured to reduce unit-incoherence.

Conservative-fallback routing: if model confidence proxy (perplexity band + heuristic signals) below threshold, route to smaller deterministic extractor or to a 'safe-mode' model that prefers omission over hallucination.
Micro-shot exemplar injection: add 1–2 tightly aligned positive and negative exemplars when the archetype is numerical-precision to anchor expected output format and rounding behavior.
short_examples: Cluster: Format-violations | Example prompt: 'Give me CSV of results' -> Model returns narrative. Patch: Format-stub scaffolding + JSON skeleton -> Valid CSV-like output increases from 32% to 87% in shadow test.
Cluster: Compound-intent | Example prompt: 'Summarize and list risks' -> Model only summarizes. Patch: Dual-funnel split into 'Write summary:' and 'List risks:' -> pass rate improves by 45%.

Cluster: Entity-misalignment | Example prompt: 'Who founded BigCorp?' -> Model attributes founder from different company. Patch: Entity-canonicalization + fuzzy match -> corrected in 71% of previously misattributed answers.
Cluster: Truncation-edge | Example prompt: long doc -> missing final paragraph facts. Patch: Context-trim + salient-prefix -> key-fact retrieval recall improved by 26%.
Cluster: Unit-incoherence | Example prompt: 'Cost: 5,000' -> Model outputs '£5,000' vs expected '$5,000'. Patch: Unit-disambiguation insertion -> failures reduced by 60%.
evaluation_results: Shadow A/B summary over 12k failing samples: overall auto-patch lift (fail->pass) 38% weighted by severity. Top lifts: format-stub (55% lift on format cluster), dual-funnel (46% lift on compound-intent). Average latency added at preprocessor layer: 12–45ms depending on patch. Human-review reduction proxy: 0.34 -> 0.21 reviews/example in shadow cohort.
rollout_plan: 1) Keep patches in shadow for 4 weeks on live onboarding traffic, measure lift and false-positive semantic drift. 2) Expose a 'soft-apply' toggle that returns both original and patched outputs to downstream devs for QA. 3) Gradually enable auto-apply for low-risk patches (punctuation-normalizer, format-stub) after approval. 4) For routing-based patches (conservative-fallback), enable canary at 2% traffic with circuit-breaker and rapid rollback hooks.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: overconstraining prompt leads to loss of creative/nuanced answers. Mitigation: keep minimal exemplars; always measure semantic-distance metric (embedding cosine) pre/post-patch. Risk: patch misfires on unseen languages or encodings. Mitigation: language detection + skip patch for non-primary locales. Risk: increased tail latencies for expensive heuristics. Mitigation: allow patch time budget; if exceeded, fallback to original request path.
next_steps: Finalize ontology labels and add 4 more rare clusters (probabilistic-coreference, idiom-misinterpretation, locale-specific-date-parsing, partial-table-merging).
Instrument per-patch 'semantic-drift' telemetry (embedding divergence + human sample audits).
Build small UI in console to toggle shadow vs auto-apply per patch and surface failing examples with label suggestions.
Add regression unit tests to onboarding harness; each patch gets 10 targeted cases and a 100-sample randomized holdout.
notes: This is intended as a living operational artifact. Keep patches as reversible transforms and prefer heuristics that are explainable. Decisions should be driven by lift vs risk; thresholds in rollout plan are intentionally conservative until we have 30k+ live examples. See linked artifacts for current implementation PRs and related Confluence write-ups.
